title: Birth in the Creole part of New Orleans and musical family
summary: Born 1899 on Villere Street in the French part of town; heard Dixieland; his uncle Emile Bigard played violin, brother Barney and cousin Natty Dominique played music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: All right, fine. Well, first thing I'd like to know is when a person's born and where?

I was born in the city of New Orleans, September 25th, 1899. In what part of town were you born? Do you remember? I mean, not as you remember, but where your folks live. In the French part of town, 1726 Northville, Creole part of town.
1726 Northville, right? Northville. I see. What kind of music did you hear when you were young?

Oh, nothing else but Dixieland music. Did your father play any instrument? I know your uncle was a violin player. You liked them low about... My uncle was a violin player. My uncle was a violin player. Well, my daddy was a... He started trumpet. But he never did violin. I know. I know. Anyone else in the family that played? Of course, we know your brother. Oh, yeah. I have a wonderful brother, Bonnie Biggoin. He's the top musician. Were there any other members of the family, any other brothers or sister that played anything? No, sir. Did your mother play or sing at any instrument? No, sir. I had a cousin that played trumpet. Natty Dominic. Oh, yes. I know him very well in Chicago. Yeah, he's in Chicago. That's right. That's the only one in my family that was playing music. I decided Professor Perron, well, he's a cousin of mine. Well, he's a cousin. Cousin of mine. Biggoin. How was he related? Was he through your mother's side of the family? Through my mother's side. Can you tell us something about your uncle? What was his name? Emile Biggoin. He was a violin player. And he was playing with Sidney Desvines Orchestra. And also he played at the West End Bungalow. Was he older than your father or younger brother? No, he was younger than my father. Way younger than my father. Who was at the West End Bungalow?
